incident-bot: Pager: P1 - Elevated serving errors and latency in eu-west (region). auto-page: maya (oncall). Rules triggered: error_rate > 10%, latency_p95 > 800ms for 5m.

maya (oncall): acked. I'm on it, will triage.

jordan (serving): I'm seeing continuous retransmit counts on IB fabric for a subset of nodes, and several serving containers OOM'ing / restarting. Logs from one pod: 
```
[serving] ERROR: CUDA out of memory while allocating 1.2GiB for logits buffer
stack: ...
[rdma] WARN: rq retries=24, failed packets=18, requeueing request
```

maya (oncall): ok, which hosts are affected? impact scope?

jordan (serving): current affected pool: serve-pool-eu-1 nodes: host-57, host-59, host-61. Traffic fallback kicked in to model-variant-small but capacity saturated; ~18% 500/502s for customer-facing endpoints. Detailed error rate per customer coming from datadog.

lee (sre): I'm seeing IB link flaps in the switch logs around 02:14 UTC. Interface counters show ECN marking and retransmits. Quick commands: 
```
# on host-57
sudo ethtool -S ib0 | grep -E "rx_err|tx_err|rnr_retry|retries"
# switch: show interface counters | include "symbol errors|link flaps"
```

sam (infra): I spun up a temporary routing policy to steer new traffic away from serve-pool-eu-1 to dedicated-secondary-eu. Pushing a canary route now (5%). If fabric keeps misbehaving we should move 100% and scale dedicated.

emily (support): Notifying affected customers in EU region. ETA for initial update 30m. Which specific endpoints?

jordan (serving): endpoints: /v1/generate (high QPS), /v1/chat (some customers). We're seeing tokenization failures on some restarts, probably due to partial model load after OOM.

maya (oncall): immediate mitigation checklist: 1) cordon affected hosts 57/59/61 2) drain pods and force-schedule elsewhere 3) enable model-variant fallback to cpu-safe variant 4) ask infra to validate IB fabric. I'll start cordon/drain.

lee (sre): I'll take fabric signal. Doing quick healthcheck: 
```
# run on host-57
ibstat -s ib0
# sample output lines
port 1: state 4 (ACTIVE)
link_downs: 3
port_errors: 42
```
This aligns with switch logs showing increased link_downs on the leaf uplink for rack-9.

sam (infra): I see correlated errors in kernel dmesg: 
```
mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: mlx5e: detected fatal RQ error, resetting device
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:81:00): 31, GPU has fallen off the bus
```
Suggest we hold on reboots until infra correlates with vendor NOC. Rebooting while fabric unstable may cause more flaps.

jordan (serving): For immediate availability I'm going to increase model-variant fallback weight to 30% and reduce max input length for heavy customers to reduce memory pressure. Deploying config change now.

incident-bot: change-log: route update applied by sam; variant fallback increased by jordan.

maya (oncall): customer impact: ~12 customers with errors above 5% (two enterprise customers in EU showing increased 502s). Emily, include those two in the initial notice; mention degraded latency and partial failures.

emily (support): acknowledging, drafting message. Will coordinate with success for targeted outreach after first update.

lee (sre): vendor NOC contacted (ticket #NOC-8821). They asked for port counters and switch uptime. I'm pulling full switch counters and attaching. Also flagged potential firmware bug for mlx5 on this hardware.

sam (infra): short-term actions: - keep cordoned nodes out of rotation - move 100% traffic off serve-pool-eu-1 by routing policy if retransmits continue for next 5m - scale up dedicated-secondary-eu by +3 replicas to absorb traffic - avoid reboots until vendor advises

maya (oncall): I'm handing to lee for oncall shift change in 20m. Lee, take the pager. I'll remain available for context.

lee (sre): I have the pager. Taking lead. Confirming current status: retran counts holding at high levels, dedicated-secondary absorbing ~65% traffic, error rate dropped to ~4.5% since partial routing.

jordan (serving): mitigation: we've also enabled prefix KV caching on the remaining healthy nodes to reduce token compute and memory pressure. Observed small improvement in p95 latencies.

sam (infra): vendor advised potential NIC fw mismatch causing ECN storm under high RDMA traffic. They want NIC fw collector logs and a core of one failing device. I'm collecting files.

lee (sre): further mitigation plan: if vendor recommends hotfix, plan controlled rolling NIC resets per rack with traffic drained first. We need runbook step: notify customers, throttle traffic, drain, reset, verify, unschedule.

maya (oncall): good. Post-incident actions to add here: - add alert for rdma_retransmit_rate > threshold - add dashboard for IB ECN marking and link_downs - update autoscaler to delay placing memory-heavy pods on nodes with recent IB errors - test fallback routing automation so we can move traffic to dedicated automatically on fabric SLO breach

emily (support): initial customer update ready. Sending now.

incident-bot: pager cleared for maya (oncall) -> pager ownership transferred to lee (sre).

lee (sre): I'll keep monitoring and coordinate the NIC fw collect. If retransmits don't improve in next 30m I'll escalate to planned rack-level NIC reset with infra.

jordan (serving): creating a postmortem ticket: INFRA-1482, will include logs, timeline, and suggested code/config mitigations (graceful fallback, aggressive caching for high mem models).

sam (infra): note: avoid immediate scale-up of GPU pods on other racks; we should verify standby NIC health first. Alternative is spinning up more dedicated CPU fallback instances for burst.

lee (sre): update 02:45 UTC: NOC replied, confirmed error signature consistent with known mlx5 fw bug. They recommend fw rollback on affected NICs as a follow-up change window. Scheduling change window with infra.

maya (oncall): thanks team. I'll label incident P1 and mark current status as "mitigated - traffic rerouted; vendor engaged; further maintenance scheduled". Leaving channel but will check updates.

emily (support): will send follow-up to customers once maintenance window is scheduled.

jordan (serving): final note — recommend adding unit tests in rollout to simulate IB retransmit bursts on canary to catch regressions that exacerbate memory pressure.

lee (sre): acknowledged. I'll draft runbook changes and schedule a postmortem meeting for tomorrow.

incident-bot: Incident P1 (1869754321) status updated -> mitigated.
